item: us_ny_post_production_credit -- rate/threshold source is secondary-corroborated (PARSED tier)
description: US_NY_POST_DOCTRINE's 35% rate and $1,000,000/75%-of-post-cost minimum-spend structure are corroborated by a secondary aggregator search, not read directly from the CT-261/IT-261 form instructions the official tax.ny.gov page defers to. Also undocumented at any tier: the exact eligible post-production expense category list beyond the VFX/animation sub-threshold, facility-location requirements, whether an annual/program cap exists, project-type eligibility, and application/preapproval process detail.
impact: None to this workstream's implementation -- the program now prices correctly using the evidence that DOES exist and disclosed producer-controlled assumptions for the rest per the global policy (Section A). A future direct read of the CT-261/IT-261 form instructions would upgrade this from PARSED to VERIFIED tier and could resolve the remaining undocumented sub-items.
recommended_next_step: A future, explicitly-scoped research workstream should fetch the actual CT-261/IT-261 form instructions directly (not the secondary aggregator) and update US_NY_POST_DOCTRINE's confidence_tier and the 5 named missing fields.

item: Fingerprint hash-randomization sensitivity (F#K Valentine's Day specifically)
description: Discovered this workstream while running the fresh final batch: current_generation_fingerprint()/evaluate_project()'s fingerprint hash for F#K Valentine's Day (and potentially other projects with similar data shape) is sensitive to Python's per-process hash randomization (PYTHONHASHSEED) -- almost certainly an unsorted set/dict somewhere in the fingerprint's input serialization specific to FVD's data shape (e.g. multilateral treaty facts). Little Utopia, Bad Hombres, and Lips Like Sugar do not exhibit this instability. Confirmed the fix: pinning PYTHONHASHSEED=0 makes the fingerprint stable and reproducible across separate process invocations.
impact: Performance/cache-efficiency only -- a cross-process fingerprint mismatch simply forces a fresh recompute (EVALUATION_COMPLETE) instead of a cache hit (EVALUATION_REUSED); it does NOT produce an incorrect priced result. Not a correctness defect. All final artifacts in this workstream used PYTHONHASHSEED=0 for reproducibility.
recommended_next_step: A future, explicitly-scoped workstream should find and sort the specific unsorted collection in FVD's fingerprint input path (likely in the multilateral/treaty-facts serialization) so the fingerprint is stable without needing to pin PYTHONHASHSEED.
